title.value: How does hemispheric specialization contribute to human-defining cognition?
title.justification: The title is explicitly mentioned at the beginning of the paper, indicating that the paper reviews the contributions of hemispheric specialization to human cognition.
title.quote: How does hemispheric specialization contribute to human-defining cognition?

analysis.description: The paper reviews the role of hemispheric specialization in human cognition, highlighting how specific local neural modules and their computational principles contribute to cognitive operations such as language, reasoning, and communication. It discusses parallels between biological neural networks and artificial neural networks, proposing that insights into brain asymmetries could inspire advancements in AI.

type.justification: The paper primarily discusses theories and concepts related to hemispheric specialization and its impact on cognition, rather than presenting empirical data or experiments.
type.quote: We propose integration of these ideas with the global workspace theory to explain dynamic relay of information products between both systems.

name.justification: The paper focuses on the neuroscience of hemispheric specialization and its implications for human cognition and artificial intelligence.
name.quote: Deepening the current understanding of how neurocognitive asymmetry makes humans special can ignite the next wave of neuroscience-inspired artificial intelligence.

name.justification: The paper discusses cognitive processes such as language and reasoning which are central to cognitive science.
name.quote: We mainly focus on language here, because it is the key faculty for human communication.

name.justification: The paper draws parallels between human brain functions and artificial neural network design, suggesting that brain asymmetry insights could inform AI development.
name.quote: We argue that insights into functional brain asymmetries could turn into a well of fresh ideas for designing the next breed of deep learning algorithms.
